_comment: Retirements of GENERATED per-project artifacts - the cleanup the upstream file compare can never name, because generated output was never a stack-shipped file. The update command applies these (with the same one-gate consent as its prune list) and validate flags them; detection is existence-based, never version math, so a leftover is caught no matter how old the install. `unwire_settings_hook` names the hook file whose settings.json entry goes, optionally scoped to one matcher as `<file>::<Matcher>` when the file stays wired for its other events. Paths resolve against the install root (the project's .claude/ parent, or the account dir in global mode); a path that does not exist simply does not detect. Every entry names why the artifact is redundant and what regenerates its replacement. Some of these act on the scope's settings.json `env` rather than on a file: `detect.settings_env_key` fires when that key is present, `detect.settings_env_value` ({key, equals}) fires only when it still holds that exact value, `rename_settings_env` ({from, to}) moves the user's VALUE to the new key and drops the old one, `remove_settings_env` ({key, when_value}) DROPS a key this stack RETIRED - nothing reads it any more, so the value is not moved anywhere; `when_value` is optional and narrows the removal to the exact value the installer itself seeded, which is what a key that still means something OUTSIDE this stack must carry, and `clear_settings_env` ({key, when_value, to}) RESETS a key whose SEEDED DEFAULT turned out to be wrong - only when the value is still that seed and the install ledger says the stack wrote it there (with no ledger, the value alone), so a value the user set by hand is never touched, one equal to the old seed included; `to` names the value it resets to (absent means empty). The installers' env pass applies the same pair on every install and update (the list is mirrored in both twins), so an env migration is REPORTED by the update command, never confirmed as a prune - nothing is deleted and a hand-set value is carried over, not reset to the default. New env keys need no entry: the installers seed them absent-only in the same pass. An entry is REMOVED from this list when the artifact it retires comes back under a new contract: `stop-contract-askuserquestion-observe-only` unwired guard-stop-contract.js's AskUserQuestion matcher because that branch DENIED mid-response; the matcher is wired again from 0.2.55 as an injection-only branch, so leaving the migration in place would have had the update unwire, in the same run, what the installer had just wired.

migrations.why: style delivery moved to the generated path-scoped project-code-style rule - the hook's injected context never reached subagent tool calls
migrations.then: re-run /capture-project-code-style so the style doc it reads from now is captured

migrations.why: the fresh-session gate fires on an ABSOLUTE token count per window tier, so a percentage of the window is not read by anything any more. It was inert at its own default on both real tiers before it was retired, and a dead key in the env block reads as a knob that still works
migrations.then: nothing - set ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FOR_1M / _FOR_300K / _FOR_200K instead, or ALFRED_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT=1 to turn the offers off

migrations.why: the window is the session model's row in the shipped hooks/model-windows.json, else ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT. The key was the first resolution layer and is read by nothing now
migrations.then: nothing - the window comes from hooks/model-windows.json, with ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT for an unlisted model; put the trigger you want in the three CONTEXT_WINDOW_FOR_* keys

migrations.why: CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE is Claude Code's own auto-compaction trigger, not a stack setting, and the installers wrote 40 into every project - a value nobody chose. It is dropped ONLY where it still holds that seed, so a value the user set by hand is theirs and stays
migrations.then: nothing - auto-compaction returns to the harness default; set the key yourself to pin a percentage

migrations.why: 2.0.0 cut the sentry MCP server from the stack (R26), and with it the headers helper this key told which auth mode to send - nothing reads it any more, and a dead key in the env block reads as a knob that still works. The account file's SENTRY_SLUG and SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN are the user's credentials and are left exactly where they are
migrations.then: nothing - to keep a Sentry server, add it yourself at the scope the install uses: claude mcp add --transport http --scope project sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp on a project install, or the same line with --scope user on a global one

migrations.why: the monitor-session hook is gone (the user's ruling of 2026-10-16): seeded `log`, its notes never reached the model, and ten days of rows (87 notes in 70 sessions - 67 of them the 80% context note fresh-session-start already covers) did not pay for the wait it added to every tool call. Nothing reads the key any more, and a dead key in the env block reads as a knob that still works
migrations.then: nothing - its old `<data root>/state/sessions/monitor-*` turn logs are inert and can be deleted by hand

migrations.why: the fresh-session triggers are named for the window tier they serve (the user's ruling of 2026-10-16): ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FOR_1M / _FOR_300K / _FOR_200K, with ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT as the window an unlisted model runs in. The value moves to the new key
migrations.then: nothing - the trigger reads ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FOR_1M

migrations.why: the fresh-session triggers are named for the window tier they serve (the user's ruling of 2026-10-16): ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FOR_1M / _FOR_300K / _FOR_200K, with ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT as the window an unlisted model runs in. The value moves to the new key; the 200K tier's seed is 180000 now, so the old seed 150000 is reset to it - a value set by hand is carried over as it is
migrations.then: nothing - the trigger reads ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FOR_200K

migrations.why: the fresh-session triggers are named for the window tier they serve (the user's ruling of 2026-10-16): ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FOR_1M / _FOR_300K / _FOR_200K, with ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT as the window an unlisted model runs in. The value moves to the new key
migrations.then: nothing - an unlisted model's window reads ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT

migrations.why: every window now takes the largest named tier it reaches (1M, 300K, else 200K) and an unlisted model runs in ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT, so no case is left for a catch-all trigger (the user's ruling of 2026-10-16). Nothing reads the key, and a dead key in the env block reads as a knob that still works
migrations.then: nothing - set ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FOR_300K for the tier an unlisted model lands on

migrations.why: three tiers at 0 turned the fresh-session offers off while ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT was a window. Now it is the trigger of a session with no tier, so the whole off switch is all four keys at 0 (2026-10-21), and an earlier 'offers off' choice would come back on an unlisted model. The DEFAULT goes to 0 while it is absent or a seed the stack wrote; a value the user typed stays
migrations.then: nothing - set ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT above 0 to have a session with no tier offered a fresh session

migrations.why: ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT is the fresh-session TRIGGER for a session whose window has no tier (the user's ruling of 2026-10-21) - an unlisted or unknown model, one under 200K, a tier variable unset or garbage - where it was the WINDOW an unlisted model was assumed to run in. The old window seed 300000 read as a trigger would sit past where a 200K or 300K model compacts, so the stack's own seed moves to 180000; a value set by hand is the user's and stays
migrations.then: nothing - the window is the model's own capacity from hooks/model-windows.json, and ALFRED_CODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_DEFAULT is the trigger when there is none

migrations.why: ALFRED_CODE_HISTORY is how many earlier sessions on the branch the start block shows (item 10 of 2026-10-21): seeded 3, up to 10, 0 off. The old on seed 1 would now show one session, so the stack's own seed moves to 3; a 1 the user typed stays
migrations.then: nothing - set ALFRED_CODE_HISTORY between 1 and 10 for more or fewer sessions, 0 for none

migrations.why: the env audit of 2026-10-21 folded the on/off keys into ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF, the one csv that already switches hooks off: the docs hook's session-start orientation block is `docs-session:block` there. A stored 0 becomes that entry; any other value was the seed's 'on' and goes. The hooks still read the old key at 0 for the 2.x line
migrations.then: nothing - add `docs-session:block` to ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF to switch it off, take it out to switch it back on
